partners.mechanism_chain: PIK3CA (HGNC:9535) —INCREASES→ PI3K-Akt-mTOR signaling pathway (KEGG:hsa04150); PI3K-Akt-mTOR signaling pathway (KEGG:hsa04150) —INCREASES→ MAPK signaling pathway (KEGG:hsa04010); MAPK signaling pathway (KEGG:hsa04010) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal T cell activation (HP:0003756); MAPK signaling pathway (KEGG:hsa04010) —LEADS_TO→ Lung cancer (MONDO:0008903). Gain-of-function mutations in PIK3CA lead to hyperactivation of the PI3K-Akt-mTOR pathway, which in turn promotes the MAPK signaling pathway. Aberrant MAPK signaling can result in abnormal T cell activation (contributing to disease A) and uncontrolled cell proliferation and survival (leading to lung cancer, disease B).

falsification.text: If mutations in PIK3CA are consistently found to be loss-of-function in disease A or have no significant impact on the MAPK signaling pathway in either disease, this hypothesis would be falsified. partners.mechanism_chain: Germline APC variant (FAP) (MONDO:0014276) —DISRUPTS→ APC (HGNC:421); APC (HGNC:421) —DISRUPTS→ Wnt signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-6811473); Wnt signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-6811473) —LEADS_TO→ Stabilization and nuclear accumulation of CTNNB1 (beta-catenin) (HP:0002660); Stabilization and nuclear accumulation of CTNNB1 (beta-catenin) (HP:0002660) —LEADS_TO→ Activation of MYC transcription (HP:0011961); Somatic APC variant (Sporadic CRC) (MONDO:0005575) —DISRUPTS→ APC (HGNC:421); Activation of MYC transcription (HP:0011961) —LEADS_TO→ Increased cell proliferation (HP:0001377); Stabilization and nuclear accumulation of CTNNB1 (beta-catenin) (HP:0002660) —LEADS_TO→ Increased cell proliferation (HP:0001377). Germline loss-of-function mutations in APC cause Familial Adenomatous Polyposis (FAP) (MONDO:0014276), characterized by numerous colorectal adenomas, a high risk of colorectal cancer. Somatic loss-of-function mutations in APC are also a frequent initiating event in sporadic colorectal cancer (MONDO:0005575). In both cases, APC dysfunction leads to the stabilization of beta-catenin (CTNNB1), which translocates to the nucleus, promoting the transcription of oncogenes like MYC and ultimately driving increased cell proliferation and tumor formation. Therefore, both diseases converge on the disruption of APC function and subsequent dysregulation of the Wnt signaling pathway, leading to increased cell proliferation.
